steps.notes: Row standardization. Target encodes ddof=0 (numpy default) — natural choice passes; ddof unstated (see minor finding).

Passes ONLY with the reverse-engineered gauge: center WITH sd-division + np.cov(ddof=1) + PCA whitening via la.eigh. Spec admits infinitely many whitenings; 5 other spec-compliant variants fail the frozen Z target.
OFFICIAL JOINT VERDICT: FAIL. Best honest implementation (bit-matches tests 0/2/3 to ~1e-14) fails test 1, whose target is a non-converged chaotic-transient snapshot. 3/4 pass under --isolate.

findings.evidence: Test 1 (the 3x8 input) target is irreproducible by any honest reimplementation. (a) The exact reverse-engineered algorithm (init w=np.random.rand(n) normalized, deflation-before-normalization, g=tanh) reproduces tests 0, 2, 3 to maxdiff ~1.8e-14 but misses test 1 by maxdiff 3.0 — the target's rows 1-2 are a ~47-degree rotation of the correct converged components inside the deflated 2D subspace. (b) The frozen target's own row 1 FAILS the prompt's convergence criterion: one further update step gives np.abs(np.abs(w @ w_new) - 1) = 3.04e-04 >> tol=1e-5, proving the reference exited via max cycles=200, not convergence. (c) Fixed-point analysis of the deflated row-1 dynamics (a circle map) shows a single stable fixed point at theta*=2.8079 with |f'| = 0.9743 — marginally stable oscillating convergence needing ~230+ iterations to reach tol from O(1); cycles=200 is insufficient by design, so the target is the iteration-200 snapshot of a still-converging trajectory 0.0124 rad short of the attractor. (d) The pre-basin transient is chaotic: a 1e-14 perturbation of the initial vector changes the termination iteration (94 -> 199) and the final direction by ~50 degrees (Lyapunov probe: separation 8e-15 -> 0.36 within 40 iterations). (e) The mathematically identical algebraic reorder of E[g'(wx)] from mean(1-g(u)**2) to 1-mean(g(u)**2) bit-matches tests 0/2/3 (1e-14) yet misses test 1 by 3.8 — bit-level evaluation order is load-bearing. Under official joint scoring one failed assert fails the whole step: steptest verdict 'RESULT step 31.3: FAIL (official joint scoring)'; --isolate shows 3/4 pass with only test 1 failing.
findings.suggested_fix: Regenerate test 1's target with parameters under which the iteration actually converges (e.g., cycles=2000, or more time samples than 8), or drop test 1, or replace the raw-matrix comparison with a gauge/transient-insensitive check (e.g., verify W @ W.T == I and that recovered components match the true sources up to sign/permutation).

findings.evidence: Tests wrap the call in np.random.seed(0), making the author's exact RNG-consumption pattern part of the frozen target, but the prompt only says 'starting from a random vector `w`'. Even for the three stable, reproducible tests (0, 2, 3), passing requires guessing all of: (1) the distribution — w = np.random.rand(nmix) per row; np.random.randn fails (maxdiff 3.3, different sign/permutation of recovered sources); (2) normalizing w at initialization, which the prompt never mentions — unnormalized rand init fails (maxdiff 4.4e-3 on test 0, well outside np.allclose); (3) the deflation step and its placement — the prompt never states the Gram-Schmidt update w_new -= W[:i].T @ (W[:i] @ w_new) (only the word 'orthogonally' hints at it), never states that w_new must be re-normalized each iteration (only inferable from the |w.w_new|~1 criterion), and applying deflation after normalization without re-normalizing (the order used in the widely-circulated Maklin ICA tutorial) fails (maxdiff 5.4e-2 to 3.8). Exactly one of the 12 structural combinations probed reproduces the targets. The prompt's update formula also contains a typo with unbalanced brackets: 'w_new = E[x g(w_curr dot x)] - w_curr E[dg (w_curr dot x]'.
findings.suggested_fix: State the full recipe in the prompt: 'initialize each row as w = np.random.rand(nmix) normalized to unit length; after each Newton update, subtract the projections onto previously found rows (w_new -= W[:i].T @ (W[:i] @ w_new)) and then normalize w_new', and fix the bracket typo. Alternatively make the test sign/permutation-invariant so the RNG path stops being part of the contract.

findings.evidence: The only stated requirement is 'Return the whitened matrix `Z`. The covariance of `Z` must be an identity matrix.' — which determines Z only up to an arbitrary orthogonal rotation — yet the test also asserts np.allclose(Z, v) against one frozen matrix. Probed six spec-compliant constructions: with center+sd preprocessing and np.cov, PCA whitening (diag(lam**-0.5) @ E.T @ Xc via la.eigh) matches the target, while ZCA whitening (E @ D^-1/2 @ E.T @ Xc — the form used in well-known ICA tutorials) and Cholesky whitening both satisfy np.cov(Z)=I to machine precision (the test's own test_identity check passes) but fail np.allclose(Z, v). Three further unstated choices are load-bearing: (a) the prompt says 'Make sure to center `X` along the rows first' but the target requires center WITH division by SD (divide_sd=True), even though step 31.1's own docstring distinguishes 'Center the input matrix X and optionally scale it by the standard deviation' — a solver reading 'center' literally (mean subtraction only) fails; (b) the covariance estimator must be ddof=1 (np.cov); the common ICA-tutorial choice C = X@X.T/n (ddof=0) yields np.cov(Z) = n/(n-1)*I ≈ 1.2*I for n=6, failing the identity check; (c) the eigh eigenvalue ordering (ascending) and LAPACK eigenvector signs fix the row order/signs of Z — an SVD-based PCA whitening (descending order) would permute rows and fail.
findings.suggested_fix: Pin the construction in the prompt/docstring: 'standardize X with center(X) (divide_sd=True); compute C = np.cov(X); eigendecompose with np.linalg.eigh; return Z = diag(eigenvalues**-0.5) @ E.T @ X_centered'. Alternatively, relax the test to gauge-invariant checks (identity covariance + Z reconstructible from X by a linear map, or compare Z.T @ Z).

findings.evidence: Prompt: 'standardize (center and divide SD) the mixture matrix `X` ... along the row'. The SD's ddof is unstated and load-bearing at the 9.5% level for the 6-10 sample test inputs: target matches X.std(axis=1) with ddof=0 (match=True) while sample SD ddof=1 fails (match=False; ratio sqrt(6/5)=1.095 >> rtol). Calibration: numpy's default std IS ddof=0, so the most natural numpy implementation passes — but ddof=1 is the default in pandas and the standard 'sample standard deviation', so a statistics-minded solver can plausibly fail. Note the internal inconsistency: step 31.2's whitening requires the ddof=1 covariance (np.cov) while this step requires ddof=0 SD.
findings.suggested_fix: Add 'use the population standard deviation (np.std default, ddof=0)' to the docstring.

overall_assessment: Not fair to score as-is. Step 31.3 is a blocker: test 1's frozen target is the max-cycles snapshot of a chaotic, non-converged iteration (the target itself violates the prompt's convergence criterion), so even a bit-faithful reimplementation that reproduces the other three tests to 1e-14 fails official joint scoring — the step is effectively unpassable. Step 31.2 is solvable only by guessing the author's whitening gauge (PCA-via-eigh + np.cov + center-with-SD) among several constructions that satisfy the stated spec exactly, and step 31.3 additionally requires guessing the unstated RNG-consumption recipe behind np.random.seed(0). Fix priority: regenerate or relax 31.3 test 1, then pin the whitening construction and the ICA initialization/deflation recipe in the prompts.
